topic: The Pi Mystery: Counting Collisions to Calculate Digits
target_audience: High school students or undergraduates with basic physics and geometry knowledge

sections.title: Introduction: The Impossible Counting Problem
lecture_lines: Imagine a tiny block hitting a massive one.
They bounce, exchanging momentum and energy.
How many collisions occur before they separate?
Surprisingly, it reveals digits of pi.
animations: Fade in text 'Imagine a tiny block hitting a massive one' color #FFFFFF.
Animate two blocks bouncing, flash #FFD700 to show momentum exchange.
Highlight collision count region with Rect stroke #00FFFF.
Fade in text 'Surprisingly, it reveals digits of pi' color #FFD700.

sections.title: Prerequisite Physics: Conservation Laws
lecture_lines: These laws dictate the collision outcomes.
animations: Display text 'Physics relies on conservation laws' color #FFFFFF.
Animate vector conservation: 'Momentum and energy stay constant' color #FFD700.
Animate vectors dictating collision outcomes using flash color #00FF00.

sections.title: Mapping Physics to Geometry: The Phase Space
lecture_lines: Map velocities to a phase plane.
animations: Display grid and text 'Map velocities to a phase plane' color #FFFFFF.
Animate trajectory 'Collisions trace a circular arc' with color #00FFFF.
Show 'The path reflects against boundaries' with color #FF4500.

sections.title: The Emergence of Pi
lecture_lines: Mass ratios define the path angle.
animations: Display circle formula, color #FFFFFF, 'Mass ratios define the path angle'.
Animate sweep: 'Paths measure the circle's arc' color #FFD700.

sections.title: Conclusion and Summary
lecture_lines: Physics acts as an analog computer.
